subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the dimensions for a brutalist slab block: roughly 48m wide, 14m deep, 27m tall with nine stories, plus a stair/lift tower, pilotis columns at ground level, and projecting concrete balcony boxes.

I'm thinking through the color palette (flat concrete tones, glass, window frames, rust accents, staying under 64 colors) and planning a box-building helper function. Now I'm working out the layout math -- column spacing for the pilotis, floor heights, bay widths, and vertical fin dividers between balcony bays to get the proportions right.

I'm estimating part counts: fins, slab projections, parapets, and roughly 384 glass/mullion window parts across 8 floors and 12 bays per side, trying to keep the total manageable while still giving the facade rhythm and some painted accent panels for color variation.

Beyond the main volume, I'm adding a windowless gable end with a vertical slit and textured mural, plus an attached stair tower at x=+27.5 with slit windows, a cantilevered crown cap, and a lift machine room on top. For the roof, I'm planning a parapet plus a few plant equipment boxes like vents and chillers to finish the massing.

On the ground level, I'm thinking of pilotis columns, a recessed glass-lobby entry core under a concrete canopy slab, and board-marked concrete texture at the podium. I'm setting floor heights at 3-unit intervals starting at y=4, with window bands centered partway up each level.

Now I'm working out the fin and loggia details on the front facade: vertical fins projecting out between bay boundaries, parapets atop each floor slab, recessed windows paired with darker door-like panels, and scattered colored infill panels placed by a modulo pattern across bays to add rhythm to the facade.

I'm cycling through a rotating five-color palette (muted ochre, rust, teal, off-white, olive) for these panels, and I estimate the total element count stays safely under 1000 if I skip mullions and just keep glass plus panels per bay per floor. I'm also confirming the end walls have narrow slit windows and that the outermost fins align with the building edges, then considering whether to add a glass lobby entrance with signage at ground level.

For the ground floor, I'm designing a recessed lobby box with glass and a canopy, and naming each structural part—facade, endWall, pilotis, fin, parapet, roofSlab—so textures and requests can target them correctly. Now I'm writing the helper function to place boxes by name, color, dimensions, and position, skipping joints since this structure is static, and adding cylinders for chimneys and a stair tower, mirroring the sides symmetrically and capping the whole thing with a roof slab at the top.

I'm laying out the roof slab and parapet dimensions covering the building's footprint, then adding rooftop plant equipment—a stair-head box, water tank, and vent cylinders—plus a lift overrun on the tower. For the tower itself, I'm positioning it to the side of the main block, spanning full height from ground to roof with vertical slit windows repeated per floor on front, back, and end faces, and capping it with a fascia slab; the tower starts right where the main block ends, with no bridge connection needed since they're adjacent.

Now I'm planning several smaller details to add: house numbers at the lobby, canopy lights, roof plant railings and an antenna, a ladder on the water tank, balcony railings with washing and plants, satellite dishes, lift signage on the tower, cable and downpipes on the end wall, glazing frames for the stair tower slits, and an entrance bench and planter at ground level.
